body:
Found republishing `UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` for #138.

## Observation

`git diff --check` reported **3,498 issues** on the republish. None were real:

```
CR-terminated lines   HEAD: 3917/3917   new: 3995/3995
file(1):              UTF-8 text, with CRLF line terminators
```

With `\r` stripped from both versions:

```
trailing space/tab lines   HEAD: 0   new: 0
git diff --check           0 issues
```

Every hit was the carriage return on a changed line — 3,498 is simply the
diff's line count. The file has been CRLF since #358 rebuilt it, and it is not
alone:

```
mappings/*.tsv with CRLF endings:  15 of 35
```

## Cause

Python's `csv.writer` defaults to `lineterminator='\r\n'`. The claw builder
that produces this file (`build_unified_ingredient_mapping.py`) and, evidently,
several of MIM's own TSV writers use that default in a repository whose other
files are LF.

## Why it matters

`git diff --check` is one of the validations PR bodies in this repo cite
(#544 listed it). On these 15 files it is not a gate — it reports every changed
line unconditionally, so a genuine trailing-space or mixed-indent defect would
be invisible inside the noise, and a reviewer either learns to ignore the
number or wastes time chasing it. I spent a cycle on it before proving the CR
was the whole story.

`--ignore-cr-at-eol` does not help: `--check` does not honour it.

## What I did not do

Not normalised in the #138 republish. Converting line endings there would turn
a 1,749/1,671-line change into a 100%-of-lines diff and bury the actual
identity corrections under whitespace churn. It wants its own commit.

## Suggested fix

- Set `lineterminator='\n'` in the writers (claw's unified-mapping builder and
  whichever MIM scripts produce the other 14), or add `*.tsv text eol=lf` to
  `.gitattributes` so git normalises on commit.
- Convert the 15 files in one dedicated whitespace-only commit so history stays
  readable, and note it in the commit message so `git blame -w` users know why.

Consumers are unaffected either way — `csv.DictReader` reads both — so this is
purely about making a stated gate mean something.
title: 15 of 35 mapping TSVs are CRLF (csv.writer default), so git diff --check flags every changed line and can't see real whitespace defects
